loadAsset.fullDescription: Loads an asset from the Unity project's AssetDatabase by its path. Optionally filters by a specific asset type. Returns the asset's name, type, path, and GUID. The asset must exist at the given path or an error is thrown. Supports all common Unity asset types including Material, Texture2D, Sprite, AudioClip, AnimationClip, GameObject, ScriptableObject, TextAsset, Font, Shader, and Mesh. If the type parameter is provided, the asset is loaded as that specific type, which can be useful when multiple asset types exist at the same path (e.g., sub-assets).

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Asset path relative to the project root (e.g., Assets/Materials/MyMaterial.mat)
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid Unity asset path starting with 'Assets/'

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Asset type name to load as. If omitted, loads as UnityEngine.Object.
parameters.constraints: Must be a recognized Unity type name (e.g., Material, Texture2D, GameObject)

workflows: Use loadAsset to verify an asset exists before modifying it with other tools.
Combine with findAssets to first search for assets, then load specific ones by path.
Use loadAsset with type parameter to confirm the asset type before performing type-specific operations.
commonErrors: ArgumentException 'Asset path is required' - The path parameter was null or empty. Provide a valid asset path.
ArgumentException 'Unknown asset type: X' - The type parameter does not match any known Unity type. Use standard Unity type names like Material, Texture2D, etc.
ArgumentException 'Asset not found at path: X' - No asset exists at the given path. Verify the path is correct and the asset has been imported.

createAsset.fullDescription: Creates a new Unity asset of the specified type at the given path. The directory is automatically created if it does not exist. The asset name is appended to the path, and a default file extension is added based on the type if the name does not already contain one. Currently supports creating Material (uses Standard shader), AnimationClip, and AnimatorController assets. After creation, the AssetDatabase is saved and refreshed.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Asset type to create (e.g., Material, AnimationClip, AnimatorController)
parameters.constraints: Must be one of the supported types: Material, AnimationClip, AnimatorController (case-insensitive)

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Directory path where the asset will be saved. The name parameter is appended to this path.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid Unity asset directory path starting with 'Assets/'

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the asset file. If no extension is included, a default extension is appended based on the type (.mat for Material, .anim for AnimationClip, .controller for AnimatorController, .asset for others).
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid file name

workflows: Create a Material asset, then use scene tools to assign it to a GameObject's renderer.
Create an AnimationClip, then create an AnimatorController to reference it.
Use findAssets first to check if a similarly named asset already exists before creating a new one.
createAsset.unityVersionNotes: Material creation uses the Standard shader, which is available in the Built-in Render Pipeline. For URP or HDRP projects, you may need to modify the material's shader after creation.
commonErrors: ArgumentException 'Type, path, and name are required' - One or more of the required parameters was null or empty. Provide all three.
ArgumentException 'Unsupported asset type: X' - The specified type is not supported for creation. Use Material, AnimationClip, or AnimatorController.
Exception 'Failed to create asset' - The asset creation process failed unexpectedly. Check the path is valid and writable.
The path parameter is the directory, not the full file path. The name is appended to path using Path.Combine.

manageAsset.fullDescription: Performs management operations on existing assets in the project. Supports three operations: 'delete' removes an asset from the project permanently. 'info' retrieves detailed information about an asset including its type, GUID, labels, dependencies, and importer settings. 'import' triggers a reimport of the asset, optionally with ForceUpdate or ForceSynchronousImport options. All operations require a valid asset path.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: Operation to perform on the asset
parameters.constraints: Must be one of: delete, info, import

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path to the asset to manage
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid Unity asset path starting with 'Assets/' pointing to an existing asset

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Import options, only used when operation is 'import'. Controls how the reimport is performed.
parameters.constraints: Must be one of: ForceUpdate, ForceSynchronousImport, or omit for default import behavior

workflows: Use 'info' operation to inspect an asset's dependencies before deleting it to avoid breaking references.
Use 'import' with ForceUpdate after externally modifying an asset file to ensure Unity picks up the changes.
Use loadAsset to verify an asset exists, then use manageAsset 'info' to get detailed metadata.
Use findAssets to locate assets, then use manageAsset 'delete' to remove unwanted ones.
commonErrors: ArgumentException 'Operation is required' - The operation parameter was null or empty.
ArgumentException 'Asset path is required' - The path parameter was null or empty.
ArgumentException 'Unknown operation: X' - The operation is not one of delete, info, or import.
ArgumentException 'Asset not found at path: X' - No asset exists at the specified path. Verify the path using findAssets or loadAsset first.
Exception 'Failed to delete asset at path: X' - The asset could not be deleted. It may be locked or in use.

findAssets.fullDescription: Searches for assets in the project using Unity's AssetDatabase.FindAssets API. Accepts a search filter string that supports type filtering (e.g., 't:Material'), name filtering, and label filtering (e.g., 'l:MyLabel'). Results can be scoped to specific folders, paginated with limit and offset, and optionally include detailed information like asset type, labels, and native asset status. In basic mode (detailed=false), only name, path, guid, and extension are returned without loading the asset, which is significantly faster for large result sets. The maximum limit is capped at 1000 to prevent excessive response sizes.

parameters.name: searchFilter
parameters.description: Search filter string using Unity's search syntax. Supports type filters (t:), label filters (l:), and name matching.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid Unity AssetDatabase search filter string

parameters.name: searchInFolders
parameters.description: Array of folder paths to restrict the search to. Each element is a string path.
parameters.constraints: Each folder path must be a valid Unity asset folder path starting with 'Assets/'

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of results to return. Capped at 1000.
parameters.constraints: Must be a positive integer. Values above 1000 are clamped to 1000.

parameters.name: offset
parameters.description: Number of results to skip for pagination.
parameters.constraints: Must be a non-negative integer

parameters.name: detailed
parameters.description: If true, loads each asset to return detailed information (type, labels, isNative). If false, returns only basic file info without loading assets.

workflows: Use findAssets with a type filter to discover all assets of a given type, then load specific ones with loadAsset.
Paginate through large result sets by using limit and offset: first call with offset=0, then offset=100, etc. Check the 'hasMore' field in the response.
Use detailed=true only when you need type and label information, as it is slower due to asset loading.
Combine findAssets with manageAsset 'info' to get full dependency information for specific assets found in the search.
commonErrors: Empty results - The search filter may be incorrect. Ensure type names match Unity types (e.g., 't:Texture2D' not 't:Texture2d'). Type names are case-sensitive in the filter.
Large response sizes - Use a smaller limit or set detailed=false for large result sets to avoid performance issues.
Invalid folder paths in searchInFolders - Folder paths must exist and start with 'Assets/'. Non-existent folders are silently ignored by Unity.

addComponent.fullDescription: Adds a Unity component to an existing GameObject in the scene. The tool searches for the component type across all loaded assemblies, starting with exact matches, then the UnityEngine namespace, and finally scanning all assemblies by short type name. If the component already exists on the target GameObject, the operation will return success=false without adding a duplicate. The scene is automatically marked dirty after a successful addition.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name or hierarchy path of the GameObject to add the component to. Uses GameObject.Find(), so a path like 'Parent/Child' can locate nested objects.
parameters.constraints: Must reference an existing active GameObject in the scene

parameters.name: componentType
parameters.description: The type name of the component to add. Can be a short name (e.g. 'Rigidbody') or a fully qualified name (e.g. 'UnityEngine.Rigidbody'). Supports both built-in Unity components and custom scripts.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid type that inherits from UnityEngine.Component

workflows: Create a physics-enabled object: use scene_createGameObject to create the object, then addComponent to add Rigidbody and a Collider (BoxCollider, SphereCollider, etc.), then setComponentProperties to configure mass, drag, and constraints.
Set up a renderable mesh: addComponent 'MeshFilter' and 'MeshRenderer' to the GameObject, then use setComponentProperties to assign a mesh and material.
Add audio to a scene object: addComponent 'AudioSource', then setComponentProperties to set clip, volume, spatial blend, and playOnAwake.
commonErrors: ERROR: 'GameObject not found' - The gameObject name/path does not match any active GameObject in the scene. Use getComponents or scene_getSceneHierarchy to verify object names.

ERROR: 'Component type not found' - The componentType string does not match any loaded type. Check spelling and ensure the assembly containing the type is loaded. Use short names like 'Rigidbody' instead of full namespaces.
RESULT: success=false with 'already exists' - The component is already attached. Use getComponents to check existing components first.
ERROR: 'Can't add component' - Some components have restrictions (e.g. only one Transform per object, or required companion components). Unity may throw if prerequisites aren't met.

removeComponent.fullDescription: Removes a component from a GameObject in the scene. The component is destroyed immediately using DestroyImmediate, which is appropriate for editor operations. The scene is automatically marked dirty after successful removal. Note that the Transform component cannot be removed from a GameObject.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name or hierarchy path of the GameObject to remove the component from. Uses GameObject.Find(), so a path like 'Parent/Child' can locate nested objects.
parameters.constraints: Must reference an existing active GameObject in the scene

parameters.name: componentType
parameters.description: The type name of the component to remove. Can be a short name or fully qualified name. The first component matching this type on the GameObject will be removed.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid Component type name. Cannot remove Transform.

workflows: Replace a component: removeComponent to remove the old one, then addComponent to add the replacement, then setComponentProperties to configure it.
Clean up unused components: use getComponents to list all components on a GameObject, then removeComponent for each unneeded one.
Switch collider types: removeComponent 'BoxCollider', then addComponent 'SphereCollider', then setComponentProperties to set the radius.
commonErrors: ERROR: 'GameObject not found' - The gameObject name/path does not match any active GameObject in the scene.
ERROR: 'Component type not found' - The componentType string does not resolve to a valid type.
RESULT: success=false with 'not found' - The specified component type is not attached to the GameObject. Use getComponents to verify.
ERROR: 'Can't destroy Transform component' - Transform is mandatory on all GameObjects and cannot be removed.
ERROR: 'Can't remove component because other components depend on it' - Other components may have RequireComponent dependencies. Remove the dependent components first.

getComponents.fullDescription: Retrieves all components attached to a GameObject, including their types, enabled state, and serialized property values. For each component, the tool returns the short type name, full type name, whether the component is enabled (for Behaviour-derived components), and a dictionary of all visible serialized properties with their current values. Property values are returned as their native types: booleans, integers, floats, strings, Vector2 {x,y}, Vector3 {x,y,z}, Color {r,g,b,a}, or the property type name as a string for unsupported types.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name or hierarchy path of the GameObject to inspect. Uses GameObject.Find(), so a path like 'Parent/Child' can locate nested objects.
parameters.constraints: Must reference an existing active GameObject in the scene

workflows: Inspect before modifying: use getComponents to see all current components and their property values, then setComponentProperties to change specific properties.
Verify component setup: after addComponent calls, use getComponents to confirm the components were added and have correct default values.
Debugging: use getComponents to inspect the full state of a problematic GameObject, checking enabled states and property values.
Pre-removal check: use getComponents to see what components exist before calling removeComponent.
commonErrors: ERROR: 'GameObject not found' - The gameObject name/path does not match any active GameObject in the scene. Verify the name using scene_getSceneHierarchy.
NOTE: Some components may show as null in the list if the underlying script is missing or the component has been destroyed but not yet cleaned up.
NOTE: Serialized properties that are complex types (ObjectReference, AnimationCurve, etc.) will be returned as their type name string rather than their actual value.

setComponentProperties.fullDescription: Sets one or more properties on a component attached to a GameObject. Supports a wide range of property types including Vector3 ({x,y,z} or [x,y,z]), Vector2 ({x,y} or [x,y]), Quaternion (via euler angles as Vector3), Color ({r,g,b,a}, hex string '#RRGGBB', or color names like 'red'), booleans, numbers, strings, enums (by name or integer), Mesh (by built-in name like 'Cube'/'Sphere' or asset path), Material (by name or asset path), and LayerMask (by layer names or integer). Dot notation is supported for nested properties (e.g. 'material.color'). Individual Vector3 components can be set via dot notation (e.g. 'localPosition.x'). When setting the Transform scale property, constrainProportionsScale is automatically enabled. Material assignments on Renderers use sharedMaterial to avoid material instance leaks in the editor.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name or hierarchy path of the GameObject. Uses a robust search that first tries GameObject.Find(), then tries path-based lookup, and finally searches all loaded objects by name.
parameters.constraints: Must reference an existing GameObject in the scene

parameters.name: componentType
parameters.description: Component type name. Common types are matched case-insensitively from a built-in dictionary (Transform, MeshRenderer, MeshFilter, Light, Camera, Rigidbody, Collider, BoxCollider, SphereCollider, CapsuleCollider, MeshCollider, AudioSource, ParticleSystem). Other types are searched across all assemblies.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid Component type that exists on the target GameObject

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: A JSON object where each key is a property name (supports dot notation for nested properties) and each value is the new property value. Multiple properties can be set in a single call. Each property is set independently, so if one fails, others may still succeed.
parameters.constraints: Property names must match actual C# property names on the component. Properties must be writable.

workflows: Position and scale a new object: after scene_createGameObject, use setComponentProperties with componentType='Transform' to set localPosition, localRotation (as euler angles), and localScale.
Set up a complete renderable: addComponent 'MeshFilter', addComponent 'MeshRenderer', then setComponentProperties on MeshFilter to set sharedMesh='Cube' and on MeshRenderer to set sharedMaterial.
Configure a light: addComponent 'Light' if needed, then setComponentProperties to set type (enum), color (hex or rgba), intensity, range, and shadows.
Configure physics: addComponent 'Rigidbody' and a collider type, then setComponentProperties on both to set mass, drag, collider size/center, isTrigger, etc.
Batch property updates: set multiple properties in a single call by passing an object with all the property key-value pairs. Each property is set independently, so partial success is possible.
setComponentProperties.unityVersionNotes: The constrainProportionsScale property on Transform (auto-enabled when setting scale) was introduced in Unity 2022.1. In earlier versions, the tool will log a warning but the scale will still be set correctly.
commonErrors: ERROR: 'GameObject not found' - The gameObject name does not match any GameObject. Check the name with scene_getSceneHierarchy.
ERROR: 'Component not found on GameObject' - The componentType is valid but not attached. Use addComponent first or check with getComponents.
ERROR: 'Property not found on [Type]' - The property name does not exist on the component. Use getComponents to see available property names. Property names are case-sensitive.
ERROR: 'Property is read-only' - Some properties (like Transform.position in certain contexts) cannot be set directly. Try the local variant (e.g. 'localPosition' instead of 'position').
ERROR: 'Invalid format for Vector3' - Vector3 values must be {x,y,z} objects or [x,y,z] arrays, not plain numbers.
ERROR: 'Invalid hex color' - Hex color strings must start with '#' followed by 6 hex digits (e.g. '#FF6600').
ERROR: 'Unknown color name' - Color name strings must match a static property on UnityEngine.Color (red, green, blue, white, black, yellow, cyan, magenta, gray, grey, clear).
ERROR: 'Mesh/Material not found' - The name doesn't match a built-in primitive (Cube, Sphere, Cylinder, Plane, Quad, Capsule) or a project asset. Check asset names with asset_findAssets.
PARTIAL SUCCESS: The results object shows per-property status. Some properties may show 'Successfully set' while others show 'Error: ...' if they failed individually.

getLogs.fullDescription: Retrieves Unity console log entries with flexible filtering options. Logs are captured in the background via Application.logMessageReceived and stored in an internal buffer (up to 1000 entries). You can filter by log type (Log, Warning, Error), search by message text, and control whether stack traces are included. Results are returned as JSON with the most recent entries last.

parameters.name: count
parameters.description: Maximum number of log entries to return. Returns the most recent entries up to this limit.
parameters.constraints: Positive integer. The internal buffer holds at most 1000 entries, so values above 1000 have no additional effect.

parameters.name: types
parameters.description: Filter logs by type. Each element is a string matching a Unity LogType. Pass 'all' to include every type. Comparison is case-insensitive.
parameters.constraints: Array of strings. Valid values: log, warning, error, assert, exception, all.

parameters.name: filterText
parameters.description: Case-insensitive substring filter applied to the log message text. Only entries whose message contains this text are returned.
parameters.constraints: Any string. Matching is case-insensitive.

parameters.name: includeStackTrace
parameters.description: When true, each log entry includes its full stack trace. When false, the stackTrace field is null.

workflows: Debugging a runtime issue: call getLogs with types=["error","exception"] and includeStackTrace=true, then use the stack trace to locate the offending script.
Monitoring play mode: call getLogs periodically with filterText set to a specific system name to watch for relevant messages.
Clean slate debugging: call clearConsole first, reproduce the issue, then call getLogs to capture only the relevant output.
commonErrors: Empty results: Logs are only captured while the MCP plugin is loaded. If the plugin was just installed, older logs will not appear.
Missing stack traces: Ensure includeStackTrace is set to true. By default stack traces are omitted to reduce payload size.
Type filter not working: Type names are case-insensitive. Use 'log', 'warning', 'error', 'assert', or 'exception'. Passing 'all' disables type filtering.

clearConsole.fullDescription: Clears the Unity Editor console window and removes all captured log entries from the internal buffer. This uses reflection to invoke UnityEditor.LogEntries.Clear(), which clears the native console, and also empties the plugin's in-memory log list. Useful before reproducing a bug so that getLogs returns only fresh entries.
workflows: Before reproducing a bug: call clearConsole, then perform the action that triggers the issue, then call getLogs to get only the relevant log output.
Routine cleanup: call clearConsole to reduce noise when the console has accumulated many irrelevant messages.
commonErrors: Reflection failure: In rare cases, Unity internal API changes may cause the LogEntries.Clear() reflection call to fail. This would result in the native console not being cleared, though the plugin's internal buffer is still emptied.

log.fullDescription: Writes a message to the Unity console with a specified log level. Supports Log, Warning, and Error types. Optionally associates the message with a context GameObject (found by name via GameObject.Find) so that clicking the log entry in the Unity console highlights the object in the hierarchy.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: The message text to write to the Unity console.
parameters.constraints: Must not be null or empty.
valueExamples: ERROR: Missing reference on Enemy prefab

parameters.name: logType
parameters.description: The severity level of the log message. Controls the icon and filtering behavior in the Unity console.
parameters.constraints: Case-insensitive. Valid values: Log, Warning, Error.

parameters.name: context
parameters.description: Name of a GameObject in the active scene to use as context. When provided, clicking the log entry in Unity's console will highlight and ping this object. Uses GameObject.Find(), so the object must be active.
parameters.constraints: Must be the name of an active GameObject in the current scene. Returns null context if not found.

workflows: Remote diagnostics: use log with logType='Warning' to flag suspicious state, then use getLogs to verify the message was recorded.
Guided debugging: log an error with a context object so the developer can click the console entry to locate the problematic GameObject.
commonErrors: Context object not found: If the context parameter names a GameObject that does not exist or is inactive, the message is still logged but without a context object. No error is thrown.
Empty message: Passing a null or empty message string will still call Debug.Log, resulting in a blank console entry.

getEditorPrefs.fullDescription: Reads a value from Unity's EditorPrefs persistent storage by key. EditorPrefs are machine-local preferences stored outside the project, commonly used for editor window states, user preferences, and plugin settings. The tool first checks whether the key exists. If it does, it attempts to read it as a string (most common type), falling back to int. If the key does not exist, the provided defaultValue is returned.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The EditorPrefs key to look up.
parameters.constraints: Must not be null or empty.

parameters.name: defaultValue
parameters.description: Value to return if the key does not exist in EditorPrefs.

workflows: Inspecting plugin configuration: call getEditorPrefs with the plugin's preference key to check current settings without opening the preferences window.
Verifying defaults: call getEditorPrefs with a defaultValue to confirm whether a preference has been explicitly set or is using the default.
commonErrors: Type mismatch: The tool tries to read the value as a string first, then falls back to int. If the value was stored as a float or bool, it may not be retrieved correctly. Use setEditorPrefs to re-set the value if needed.
Key not found without default: If the key does not exist and no defaultValue is provided, the result will have exists=false and value=null.
Empty key: Passing a null or empty key string throws an ArgumentException.

setEditorPrefs.fullDescription: Sets a value in Unity's EditorPrefs persistent storage. The value type is automatically detected from the JSON token type: strings are stored via SetString, integers via SetInt, floats via SetFloat, booleans via SetBool. Other types are converted to string. EditorPrefs persist across Unity sessions and are stored per-machine (not in the project).

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The EditorPrefs key to set.
parameters.constraints: Must not be null or empty.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to store. The type is inferred from the JSON value: string, integer, float, or boolean. Other types are stored as their string representation.
parameters.constraints: Must not be null.

workflows: Configuring a plugin remotely: use setEditorPrefs to change settings, then verify with getEditorPrefs.
Resetting preferences: set a key to its default value to reset a plugin's configuration without opening the preferences UI.
Toggling features: use setEditorPrefs with a boolean value to enable or disable editor features.
commonErrors: Null value: Passing a null value throws an ArgumentException. Always provide a valid value.
Empty key: Passing a null or empty key string throws an ArgumentException.
Type not preserved: If you set a value as a float but later read it with getEditorPrefs, the current implementation reads strings first. Consider the read-back behavior when choosing types.

pauseEditor.fullDescription: Pauses or unpauses the Unity Editor. When paused, the game simulation freezes (equivalent to pressing the Pause button in the toolbar). This only has a visible effect when the Editor is in Play mode. Setting isPaused while not in Play mode will take effect the next time Play mode is entered.

parameters.name: pause
parameters.description: True to pause the editor, false to unpause (resume) it.
parameters.constraints: Must be a boolean value.

workflows: Freeze-frame debugging: call pauseEditor with pause=true during Play mode, inspect the scene state, then call pauseEditor with pause=false to resume.
Conditional breakpoint: use getLogs to monitor for a specific error, then call pauseEditor to freeze the simulation when the error is detected.
Step-by-step testing: pause the editor, make scene modifications, then unpause to observe the effect frame by frame.
commonErrors: No visible effect: If the editor is not in Play mode, setting pause=true will not visibly pause anything. The pause state is applied when Play mode is next entered.
Already in requested state: Calling pause=true when already paused (or pause=false when already running) is a no-op. The response still indicates success with the current isPaused state.

executeMenuItem.fullDescription: Executes a Unity Editor menu item by its full menu path. This triggers the same action as clicking the menu item in the Unity Editor UI. The menu item must exist and be valid; otherwise an error is returned. Useful for automating editor workflows such as creating assets, opening windows, running build pipelines, or invoking custom editor extensions registered under the menu bar.

parameters.name: menuPath
parameters.description: The full menu item path as it appears in the Unity Editor menu bar, using '/' as separator.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid, existing menu path. Case-sensitive.

workflows: Create a new material: executeMenuItem('Assets/Create/Material') -> then use asset tools to configure it.
Add a primitive to the scene: executeMenuItem('GameObject/3D Object/Cube') -> then use scene tools to position it.
Save the project after making changes: Use scene/asset tools to modify content -> executeMenuItem('File/Save Project').
executeMenuItem.unityVersionNotes: Menu paths may differ between Unity versions. Some menu items are only available in specific Unity versions or when certain packages are installed.
commonErrors: Error: 'Failed to execute menu item: <path>' - The menu path does not exist or is disabled. Verify the exact path by checking the Unity Editor menu bar.
Error: 'Menu path is required' - The menuPath parameter was not provided or was empty.
Some menu items require a specific context (e.g., a selected object) to be enabled. Ensure prerequisites are met before execution.

getSelection.fullDescription: Retrieves information about the currently selected objects in the Unity Editor. Returns details about selected GameObjects in the scene hierarchy and selected assets in the Project window, including names, paths, types, instance IDs, and GUIDs. This is useful for inspecting what the user has selected before performing operations on those objects.
workflows: Inspect selection before modification: getSelection() -> read the selected objects -> use scene tools to modify components on the selected GameObjects.
Get selected assets for batch processing: getSelection() -> iterate returned asset paths -> use asset tools to process each asset.
Verify selection after setSelection: setSelection({objects: [...]}) -> getSelection() to confirm the selection was applied correctly.
commonErrors: Returns empty arrays if nothing is selected. This is not an error; it simply means no objects are currently selected in the Editor.
Assets in the Project window may not appear in the gameObjects array; they appear in the assets array instead.

setSelection.fullDescription: Sets the current selection in the Unity Editor to the specified objects. Accepts an array of object identifiers which can be GameObject names, full hierarchy paths, or asset paths. The tool first tries to find each identifier as a GameObject by path (using GameObject.Find), then as an asset path (using AssetDatabase), and finally searches all loaded GameObjects by name. Pass an empty array to clear the selection.

parameters.name: objects
parameters.description: Array of names or paths of objects to select. Each entry can be a GameObject name, a hierarchy path (e.g., 'Parent/Child'), or an asset path (e.g., 'Assets/Materials/MyMat.mat').
parameters.constraints: Must be an array of strings. Pass an empty array to clear the selection.

workflows: Select objects before inspection: setSelection({objects: ['Player']}) -> use getSelection() or scene tools to inspect the object's components.
Select an asset for modification: setSelection({objects: ['Assets/Materials/MyMat.mat']}) -> use asset tools to modify the asset.
Clear selection: setSelection({objects: []}) to deselect everything.
commonErrors: selectedCount is 0 even though objects were specified - The object names/paths could not be found. Ensure the names match exactly (case-sensitive) and that GameObjects are active in the scene.
GameObject.Find only finds active GameObjects. Inactive GameObjects are searched via Resources.FindObjectsOfTypeAll as a fallback, but only if they have a valid scene.
If an object cannot be found by any method, it is silently skipped. Check the selectedCount in the response to verify how many objects were actually selected.

getProjectSettings.fullDescription: Retrieves Unity project settings for a specified category. Supports 'Player', 'Graphics', 'Quality', 'Resolution', and general settings. When no category is specified or an unrecognized category is given, returns general project information including Unity version, platform, build target, and scripting backend. This tool is read-only and does not modify any settings.

parameters.name: category
parameters.description: Settings category to retrieve. Supported values: 'Player', 'Graphics', 'Quality', 'Resolution'. Any other value returns general project settings.
parameters.constraints: Case-insensitive. Unrecognized categories fall back to general settings.

workflows: Check project configuration: getProjectSettings({category: 'Player'}) to review company name, product name, and application identifier.
Verify rendering settings: getProjectSettings({category: 'Graphics'}) to check color space and GPU skinning configuration.
Audit quality settings: getProjectSettings({category: 'Quality'}) to review quality levels, VSync, and anti-aliasing settings.
Check resolution settings: getProjectSettings({category: 'Resolution'}) to review screen dimensions, fullscreen mode, and current Game view size.
Get general project info: getProjectSettings({}) or getProjectSettings({category: 'General'}) to retrieve Unity version, build target, and scripting backend.
getProjectSettings.unityVersionNotes: Some PlayerSettings properties may be deprecated or unavailable in newer Unity versions. The scripting backend retrieval uses EditorUserBuildSettings.selectedBuildTargetGroup which may behave differently across Unity versions.
commonErrors: Unrecognized category names do not produce an error; they return general project settings instead. Ensure you use 'Player', 'Graphics', or 'Quality' for specific settings.
This tool is read-only. To modify project settings, use executeMenuItem to open the appropriate settings window.

refresh.fullDescription: Refreshes the Unity AssetDatabase, causing Unity to re-scan and re-import any changed assets. The refresh is performed via EditorApplication.delayCall to ensure the response is sent before a potential Domain Reload. This is essential after modifying files on disk (e.g., creating or editing scripts, textures, or other assets) to make Unity recognize the changes. Warning: if script files have been modified, this may trigger a Domain Reload which temporarily interrupts the editor.

parameters.name: importOptions
parameters.description: Import options controlling how the refresh is performed.
parameters.constraints: Must be one of: 'Default', 'ForceUpdate', 'ForceSynchronousImport'. Any other value uses default behavior.

workflows: After creating/modifying files on disk: Write files via filesystem tools -> refresh() to make Unity recognize the changes.
Force reimport of changed assets: refresh({importOptions: 'ForceUpdate'}) to ensure all changed assets are reimported.
Synchronous refresh for immediate availability: refresh({importOptions: 'ForceSynchronousImport'}) when you need assets to be available immediately after the call.
refresh.unityVersionNotes: Domain Reload behavior may vary between Unity versions. Unity 2019.3+ supports 'Enter Play Mode Options' which can affect reload behavior.
commonErrors: The tool may report success but Unity may trigger a Domain Reload shortly after, which can interrupt MCP communication. The response includes 'mayTriggerReload: true' as a warning.
If scripts have compilation errors, the refresh will still proceed but Unity will show errors in the Console.
ForceSynchronousImport can cause the editor to freeze briefly while importing large numbers of assets.

clearConsole.fullDescription: Clears all log messages from the Unity Console window. Uses reflection to invoke the internal UnityEditor.LogEntries.Clear() method. This removes all Debug.Log, Debug.LogWarning, and Debug.LogError messages from the console. Useful for cleaning up the console before running a specific operation to isolate new log output.
workflows: Clean console before testing: clearConsole() -> enterPlayMode({enter: true}) -> check console logs for errors.
Clear before compilation: clearConsole() -> compileScripts() -> check for compilation warnings/errors in a clean console.
clearConsole.unityVersionNotes: Uses reflection to access UnityEditor.LogEntries.Clear(). The internal API name may change in future Unity versions, though it has been stable across Unity 2019-2023.
commonErrors: Error: 'Failed to clear console: ...' - The reflection-based approach failed, possibly due to an internal API change in the Unity version being used.
This tool returns success: false (not an exception) if the clear operation fails, so always check the success field in the response.

compileScripts.fullDescription: Requests Unity to recompile all scripts in the project. Internally calls AssetDatabase.Refresh() followed by EditorUtility.RequestScriptReload(), both deferred via EditorApplication.delayCall to ensure the response is sent before the Domain Reload occurs. If scripts are already compiling, the request is rejected. After compilation, Unity performs a Domain Reload which reloads all managed assemblies and reinitializes the editor state.
workflows: After editing script files: Modify .cs files via filesystem tools -> compileScripts() to compile and reload.
Verify compilation: compileScripts() -> wait for reload -> getEditorInfo() to check isCompiling status.
Full workflow: Edit scripts -> compileScripts() -> clearConsole() -> enterPlayMode({enter: true}) to test changes.
compileScripts.unityVersionNotes: Domain Reload behavior depends on Unity version and project settings. Unity 2019.3+ supports disabling Domain Reload in Enter Play Mode Settings, but compileScripts still triggers a reload.
commonErrors: Error: 'Scripts are already compiling' - Unity is currently in the middle of a compilation. Wait for the current compilation to finish before requesting another.
The response includes 'willCauseReload: true' to indicate that a Domain Reload will occur shortly. MCP communication may be temporarily interrupted.
If there are compilation errors in scripts, Unity will report them in the Console but the tool call itself will succeed.

enterPlayMode.fullDescription: Enters or exits Unity Play Mode. When entering play mode, Unity initializes the game runtime and starts executing game scripts. When exiting, Unity stops the game and restores the editor state. The tool checks the current play state before acting: if already in the requested state, it does nothing but still returns success. The response includes the current isPlaying and isPaused status after the operation.

parameters.name: enter
parameters.description: True to enter play mode, false to exit play mode.
parameters.constraints: Must be a boolean value.

workflows: Test gameplay: Set up scene with scene tools -> enterPlayMode({enter: true}) -> observe behavior -> enterPlayMode({enter: false}).
Quick play test: clearConsole() -> enterPlayMode({enter: true}) -> check console logs for runtime errors -> enterPlayMode({enter: false}).
Compile and test: compileScripts() -> wait for reload -> enterPlayMode({enter: true}).
enterPlayMode.unityVersionNotes: EditorApplication.EnterPlaymode() and ExitPlaymode() are available in Unity 2019.1+. In older versions, EditorApplication.isPlaying was set directly.
commonErrors: Entering play mode may fail silently if there are compilation errors. Check isCompiling via getEditorInfo() before entering play mode.
Play mode transitions are not instantaneous. The isPlaying state in the response reflects the state at the time of the call, which may not yet reflect the transition.
Scene changes made during play mode are lost when exiting play mode. This is standard Unity behavior.

getEditorInfo.fullDescription: Retrieves comprehensive information about the current state of the Unity Editor. Returns the Unity version, editor platform, active build target, play mode status, compilation status, time since editor startup, and key project paths (project path, temporary cache path, persistent data path). This is a read-only informational tool useful for diagnostics and understanding the current editor state.
workflows: Pre-flight check: getEditorInfo() to verify Unity version and build target before performing platform-specific operations.
Check editor state: getEditorInfo() to check isPlaying, isPaused, and isCompiling before performing operations that require specific states.
Get project paths: getEditorInfo() to retrieve projectPath for file system operations relative to the Unity project.
commonErrors: This tool is read-only and should not produce errors under normal circumstances.
The timeSinceStartup value represents editor uptime in seconds and resets when the editor restarts.

createGameObject.fullDescription: Creates a new empty GameObject in the current scene. You can specify a name, an optional parent (by path or name), and an optional world position. The new GameObject will be parented under the specified parent if provided. The scene is automatically marked dirty after creation. Returns the created GameObject's name, instanceId, hierarchy path, and detailed data.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the GameObject to create.
parameters.constraints: Must be a non-empty string.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Path or name of the parent GameObject. The new object will be parented under this object. Supports hierarchy paths (e.g. 'Canvas/Panel') or simple names (e.g. 'Canvas'). If not found or omitted, the object is created at the scene root.
parameters.constraints: Must reference an existing GameObject in the scene.

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: World position for the new GameObject as a Vector3 with x, y, z properties.
parameters.constraints: Must be an object with numeric x, y, z properties.

workflows: Create a GameObject, then use setGameObjectProperties to set rotation, scale, tag, or layer.
Create a GameObject, then use component tools (e.g. component_addComponent) to add Rigidbody, Collider, or custom scripts.
Create multiple GameObjects with parent references to build a hierarchy: create parent first, then children referencing the parent path.
commonErrors: Parent not found: The parent path or name does not match any existing GameObject. The object will be created at root level. Verify the parent exists using manageGameObject with operation 'find'.
Empty name: The name parameter is required and must be non-empty.
Position format: The position must be an object with x, y, z numeric properties, not an array or single number.

manageGameObject.fullDescription: Performs management operations on an existing GameObject: 'find' to locate it and return basic info (name, instanceId, path, active state, tag, layer), 'delete' to destroy it immediately (DestroyImmediate), or 'info' to get detailed information including transform data, components, child count, and parent. GameObjects can be referenced by name or hierarchy path. The search checks active objects first via GameObject.Find, then searches all objects (including inactive) by name, then by full path.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: Operation to perform on the GameObject.
parameters.constraints: Must be one of: 'find', 'delete', 'info'.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name or hierarchy path of the target GameObject. Supports both simple names (e.g. 'Player') and full hierarchy paths (e.g. 'Environment/Props/Tree').
parameters.constraints: Must match an existing GameObject. For inactive objects, use the full hierarchy path.

workflows: Use 'find' to verify a GameObject exists before performing other operations on it.
Use 'info' to inspect a GameObject's components and transform before modifying properties with setGameObjectProperties.
Use 'delete' to remove temporary or unwanted objects, then create replacements with createGameObject.
commonErrors: GameObject not found: The name or path does not match any object in the scene. Check spelling, case sensitivity, and hierarchy path. Inactive objects may not be found by simple name -- use the full hierarchy path.
Operation is required: The 'operation' parameter must be provided and must be one of 'find', 'delete', or 'info'.
Unknown operation: Only 'find', 'delete', and 'info' are supported. The operation string is case-insensitive.
Deleting a parent: Deleting a GameObject also destroys all of its children. This cannot be undone at runtime.

setActive.fullDescription: Sets a GameObject's active/inactive state using SetActive(). An inactive GameObject and all its children are disabled in the scene -- they will not render, receive updates, or respond to physics. Returns the previous and current active states for confirmation. The GameObject is found by name or hierarchy path, searching active objects first then inactive ones.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name or hierarchy path of the target GameObject.
parameters.constraints: Must match an existing GameObject in the scene.

parameters.name: active
parameters.description: True to activate the GameObject, false to deactivate it.
parameters.constraints: Must be a boolean value (true or false).

workflows: Deactivate a UI panel to hide it, then reactivate it later to show it.
Use manageGameObject with operation 'find' to locate the object first, then use setActive to toggle its state.
Deactivate objects to temporarily exclude them from the scene without deleting them.
commonErrors: GameObject not found: The specified name or path does not match any object. If the object is already inactive, use its full hierarchy path to find it.
Children also affected: Deactivating a parent implicitly hides all children. Children's own activeSelf state is preserved, but they become inactive in the hierarchy.
GameObject name is required: The 'gameObject' parameter must be a non-empty string.

setGameObjectProperties.fullDescription: Sets multiple properties on a GameObject in a single call. Supports transform properties (position, rotation, scale), object state (active, name, tag, layer), and per-component Vector3 access (e.g. 'position.x', 'scale.y'). Position and rotation use world space. Scale sets localScale. When setting scale, constrainProportionsScale is automatically enabled on the transform. Each property is set independently and errors on one property do not prevent others from being applied. The scene is marked dirty after all properties are set.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name or hierarchy path of the target GameObject.
parameters.constraints: Must match an existing GameObject in the scene.

parameters.name: properties
parameters.description: An object containing the properties to set. Supported keys: 'position' (Vector3 {x,y,z}), 'rotation' (Vector3 euler angles {x,y,z}), 'scale' or 'localScale' (Vector3 {x,y,z} or uniform number), 'active' (bool), 'name' (string), 'tag' (string), 'layer' (string name or int index). Also supports dot-notation for individual Vector3 components: 'position.x', 'position.y', 'position.z', 'rotation.x', 'rotation.y', 'rotation.z', 'scale.x', 'scale.y', 'scale.z'.
parameters.constraints: Must be a non-empty object. Vector3 values accept {x,y,z} objects or [x,y,z] arrays. Scale also accepts a single number for uniform scaling. Tag must be a valid Unity tag. Layer must be a valid layer name or index (0-31).

workflows: Create a GameObject with createGameObject, then immediately set its properties (tag, layer, rotation, scale) with setGameObjectProperties.
Use manageGameObject with operation 'info' to inspect current transform values, then use setGameObjectProperties to adjust them.
Set position.x or position.y individually to slide an object along a single axis without affecting other axes.
Set scale to a uniform number (e.g. 2) to scale proportionally, or use a Vector3 for non-uniform scaling.
setGameObjectProperties.unityVersionNotes: The constrainProportionsScale property on Transform is automatically enabled when setting scale. This property is available in Unity 2022.1+. In older versions, a warning is logged but scale is still applied.
commonErrors: GameObject not found: The specified name or path does not match any object in the scene. Verify the object exists using manageGameObject with operation 'find'.

Invalid Vector3 format: Position and rotation must be objects with x, y, z numeric properties (e.g. {"x": 0, "y": 1, "z": 0}) or arrays with 3 elements (e.g. [0, 1, 0]). Single numbers are only accepted for scale.
Invalid layer: The layer name does not exist in the project's layer settings. Use a valid layer name (e.g. 'Default', 'UI') or layer index (0-31).
Invalid tag: The tag must be defined in Unity's Tag Manager (Edit > Project Settings > Tags and Layers). Use manageGameObject with operation 'info' to check the current tag.

Unknown property: Properties not matching any known key (position, rotation, scale, localScale, active, name, tag, layer) or valid dot-notation (e.g. position.x) will be reported as 'Unknown property' in the results.
Properties object is required: The 'properties' parameter must be a non-null JSON object with at least one key.

createPrefab.fullDescription: Creates a new prefab asset from an existing GameObject in the current scene. The GameObject is saved as a prefab at the specified path and automatically connected to the new prefab asset (using SaveAsPrefabAssetAndConnect). If the target directory does not exist, it will be created automatically. After creation, the original GameObject becomes a prefab instance linked to the newly created prefab asset.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name or path of the GameObject in the current scene to convert into a prefab. Uses GameObject.Find() internally, so the name must match an active GameObject in the scene.
parameters.constraints: Must reference an existing active GameObject in the currently loaded scene.

parameters.name: prefabPath
parameters.description: The asset path where the prefab will be saved. Must start with 'Assets/' and end with '.prefab'.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid Unity asset path starting with 'Assets/' and ending with '.prefab'.

workflows: Build a GameObject in the scene with components, then call createPrefab to persist it as a reusable asset.
After createPrefab, use instantiatePrefab to place additional instances of the same prefab in the scene.
Combine with scene and gameObject tools: create a GameObject, add components, position it, then save as prefab.
createPrefab.unityVersionNotes: Uses PrefabUtility.SaveAsPrefabAssetAndConnect which is available in Unity 2018.3 and later. The nested prefab workflow was introduced in Unity 2018.3.
commonErrors: "GameObject 'X' not found" -- The specified GameObject does not exist or is inactive in the current scene. Ensure it is active and the name is correct.
"Failed to create prefab" -- The prefab could not be saved. Check that the prefabPath is a valid asset path and that the project is not in a read-only state.
Invalid prefabPath not starting with 'Assets/' will cause Unity to fail silently or throw an internal error.

instantiatePrefab.fullDescription: Instantiates an existing prefab asset into the currently active scene, maintaining the prefab link. The instance is placed at the specified world position (defaults to origin if not provided) and can optionally be parented to another GameObject. The scene is automatically marked as dirty after instantiation so changes can be saved.

parameters.name: prefabPath
parameters.description: The asset path of the prefab to instantiate. Must point to an existing .prefab file in the project.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid asset path to an existing prefab (e.g., 'Assets/Prefabs/MyPrefab.prefab').

parameters.name: position
parameters.description: World position to place the instantiated prefab. An object with x, y, z number fields.
parameters.constraints: Each coordinate (x, y, z) should be a valid number. Missing coordinates default to 0.

parameters.name: parent
parameters.description: Name of an existing GameObject in the scene to set as the parent of the instantiated prefab. Uses GameObject.Find() so the parent must be active in the scene.
parameters.constraints: If provided, must match the name of an active GameObject in the scene. Silently ignored if the parent is not found.

workflows: Use createPrefab first to create the prefab asset, then instantiatePrefab to place multiple copies in the scene.
Instantiate a UI prefab and parent it to a Canvas for runtime UI construction.
Populate a scene by calling instantiatePrefab multiple times with different positions to lay out environment objects.
instantiatePrefab.unityVersionNotes: Uses PrefabUtility.InstantiatePrefab which maintains the prefab connection, unlike UnityEngine.Object.Instantiate which breaks it.
commonErrors: "Prefab not found at path: X" -- The specified prefabPath does not point to a valid prefab asset. Verify the path is correct and the asset exists.
If the parent GameObject is not found, the prefab is still instantiated but placed at the scene root without error.
NullReferenceException may occur if the prefab asset is corrupted or missing its root GameObject.

applyPrefabChanges.fullDescription: Applies all override changes from a prefab instance in the scene back to its source prefab asset. This permanently modifies the prefab asset on disk, and all other instances of the same prefab across all scenes will inherit the applied changes. The operation uses PrefabUtility.ApplyPrefabInstance with UserAction interaction mode.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name of the prefab instance in the current scene whose overrides should be applied to the prefab asset.
parameters.constraints: Must be an active GameObject that is a prefab instance (not an unpacked or regular GameObject).

workflows: Modify a prefab instance in the scene (e.g., change transform, add components), then call applyPrefabChanges to persist those modifications to the prefab asset.
Use with instantiatePrefab: instantiate a prefab, make changes to the instance, then apply changes so all future instances reflect the update.
Before applying, you can use revertPrefabChanges to undo unwanted modifications on the instance.
applyPrefabChanges.unityVersionNotes: Uses PrefabUtility.ApplyPrefabInstance available in Unity 2018.3+. In nested prefab workflows, this applies overrides to the nearest prefab asset root.
commonErrors: "GameObject 'X' not found" -- The specified GameObject does not exist or is inactive. Ensure it is active in the scene.
"GameObject 'X' is not a prefab instance" -- The GameObject is either a regular scene object or has been unpacked. Only connected prefab instances can apply changes.
If the prefab asset is read-only or locked by version control, the apply operation may fail.

revertPrefabChanges.fullDescription: Reverts all override changes on a prefab instance, restoring it to match the source prefab asset exactly. This discards any modifications made to the instance (added/removed components, property changes, etc.) and resets it to the state defined by the prefab asset. Uses PrefabUtility.RevertPrefabInstance with UserAction interaction mode.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name of the prefab instance in the current scene to revert back to the prefab asset state.
parameters.constraints: Must be an active GameObject that is a connected prefab instance.

workflows: After experimenting with changes on a prefab instance, call revertPrefabChanges to discard all modifications and reset to the original prefab state.
Use as a safety measure before applyPrefabChanges on a different instance, to ensure a clean state.
Combine with scene tools: inspect the scene hierarchy, identify modified prefab instances, and selectively revert them.
revertPrefabChanges.unityVersionNotes: Uses PrefabUtility.RevertPrefabInstance available in Unity 2018.3+. For nested prefabs, this reverts overrides on the outermost prefab instance.
commonErrors: "GameObject 'X' not found" -- The specified GameObject does not exist or is inactive. Ensure it is active in the scene.
"GameObject 'X' is not a prefab instance" -- The GameObject is not a connected prefab instance. Regular GameObjects or fully unpacked prefabs cannot be reverted.
Reverting does not undo scene-level changes like reparenting. If the instance was moved to a different parent, the parent change is also reverted.

unpackPrefab.fullDescription: Unpacks a prefab instance, breaking the connection between the scene instance and the prefab asset. Supports two unpack modes: 'OutermostRoot' which only unpacks the outermost prefab while keeping nested prefabs intact, and 'Completely' which recursively unpacks all nested prefabs turning everything into regular GameObjects. The scene is automatically marked as dirty after unpacking.

parameters.name: gameObject
parameters.description: Name of the prefab instance in the scene to unpack.
parameters.constraints: Must be an active GameObject that is a connected prefab instance.

parameters.name: unpackMode
parameters.description: Determines how deeply to unpack the prefab. 'OutermostRoot' unpacks only the top-level prefab, preserving nested prefab connections. 'Completely' recursively unpacks all nested prefabs.
parameters.constraints: Must be either 'OutermostRoot' or 'Completely'. Any other value is treated as 'Completely'.

workflows: Unpack a prefab instance to freely modify its hierarchy without affecting the original prefab asset.
Use 'OutermostRoot' mode to unpack the top-level prefab while preserving nested prefab references for partial customization.
After unpacking, the GameObjects become regular scene objects. Use createPrefab to save the modified hierarchy as a new prefab if needed.
unpackPrefab.unityVersionNotes: Uses PrefabUtility.UnpackPrefabInstance available in Unity 2018.3+. The OutermostRoot mode is particularly useful with nested prefabs introduced in Unity 2018.3.
commonErrors: "GameObject 'X' not found" -- The specified GameObject does not exist or is inactive. Ensure it is active in the scene.
"GameObject 'X' is not a prefab instance" -- The GameObject has already been unpacked or was never a prefab instance.
Once unpacked, the operation cannot be undone via revertPrefabChanges. Use Edit > Undo (Ctrl+Z) in the Unity Editor if needed.

createFolder.fullDescription: Creates a new folder in the Unity project's Assets directory. The folder is created using AssetDatabase.CreateFolder, which properly registers it with Unity's asset pipeline. If the folder already exists at the specified path, the operation will return a failure message without throwing an error. The parent folder path must already exist. After creation, AssetDatabase.Refresh() is called to update the editor.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Parent folder path where the new folder will be created. Must be an existing folder under Assets.
parameters.constraints: Must start with 'Assets' and the parent folder must already exist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the new folder to create.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid folder name. Avoid special characters that are invalid in file system paths.

workflows: Use createFolder to set up project directory structure, then use createScript to add scripts to the created folders.
Use getProjectStructure first to inspect existing folders, then createFolder to add missing directories.
Create a folder hierarchy by calling createFolder multiple times: first create the parent, then the child folders.
commonErrors: Error: 'Parent path and folder name are required' - Ensure both 'path' and 'name' parameters are provided and non-empty.
Error: 'Folder already exists' - The folder at the combined path already exists. Use getProjectStructure to check before creating.
Error: 'Failed to create folder' - The parent path does not exist or is invalid. Create parent folders first.

deleteFolder.fullDescription: Deletes a folder from the Unity project using AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset. This removes the folder and all its contents (files and subfolders) permanently. The deletion is registered with Unity's asset pipeline, and associated .meta files are also removed. After deletion, AssetDatabase.Refresh() is called to update the editor. This operation cannot be undone.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The full path of the folder to delete, relative to the project root.
parameters.constraints: Must start with 'Assets' and must be a valid existing folder path.

workflows: Use getProjectStructure to identify folders to delete, then call deleteFolder to remove them.
Before deleting, use findAssets (from asset tools) to check if the folder contains important assets.
commonErrors: Error: 'Folder path is required' - The 'path' parameter was not provided or is empty.
Error: 'Folder not found' - The specified folder does not exist. Verify the path with getProjectStructure.
Error: 'Failed to delete folder' - The folder may be locked by another process or contain read-only files.

manageAssetFile.fullDescription: Manages asset file operations including move, rename, and duplicate. All operations use Unity's AssetDatabase API to ensure proper asset pipeline handling, including updating .meta files, references, and GUIDs. The 'move' operation moves an asset to a new path. The 'rename' operation renames an asset in place (without changing its directory). The 'duplicate' operation creates a copy of an asset; if no destination path is specified, a '_copy' suffix is appended to the original filename.

parameters.name: operation
parameters.description: The file operation to perform.
parameters.constraints: Must be one of: 'move', 'rename', 'duplicate'.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The source asset path. For all operations, this is the current path of the asset.
parameters.constraints: Must start with 'Assets' and point to an existing asset file.

parameters.name: newPath
parameters.description: The destination path for move and duplicate operations. For move, this is the full new path including filename. For duplicate, if omitted, a '_copy' suffix is used.
parameters.constraints: Required for 'move' operation. Optional for 'duplicate'. Not used for 'rename'. Must include filename and extension.

parameters.name: newName
parameters.description: The new name for the rename operation, without the file extension.
parameters.constraints: Required for 'rename' operation. Do not include the file extension.

workflows: Use findAssets (from asset tools) to locate an asset, then manageAssetFile to move or rename it.
Use getProjectStructure to plan a reorganization, then createFolder to set up new directories, then manageAssetFile with 'move' to relocate assets.
Duplicate a prefab with manageAssetFile, then modify the duplicate's components using scene/gameObject tools.
commonErrors: Error: 'Operation is required' - The 'operation' parameter was not provided.
Error: 'Asset path is required' - The 'path' parameter was not provided or is empty.
Error: 'newPath is required for move operation' - When using 'move', you must provide the 'newPath' parameter.
Error: 'newName is required for rename operation' - When using 'rename', you must provide the 'newName' parameter.
Error: 'Failed to move asset' / 'Failed to rename asset' - The source asset does not exist, the destination already exists, or the destination folder does not exist.
Error: 'Unknown operation' - The operation must be exactly 'move', 'rename', or 'duplicate' (case-insensitive).

getProjectStructure.fullDescription: Retrieves the folder structure of the Unity project as a hierarchical tree. Starting from a specified root path, it traverses directories up to a configurable maximum depth. Optionally includes files in the output (excluding hidden files and .meta files). Hidden folders (starting with '.') are automatically excluded. Each node in the returned structure includes the name, type ('folder' or 'file'), and path. Folders that exceed the maximum depth are marked with 'truncated: true'.

parameters.name: rootPath
parameters.description: The root path to start traversing from.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid folder path within the project.

parameters.name: includeFiles
parameters.description: Whether to include files in the structure output. When false, only folders are returned.

parameters.name: maxDepth
parameters.description: Maximum depth of folder traversal. Higher values return more detail but take longer.
parameters.constraints: Should be a positive integer. Very high values may produce large responses.

workflows: Call getProjectStructure first to understand the project layout before creating new folders or scripts.
Use getProjectStructure with includeFiles=true and a specific rootPath to find files in a particular directory.
Use getProjectStructure with maxDepth=1 for a quick overview of top-level folders, then drill down with a more specific rootPath.
commonErrors: Empty structure returned - The specified rootPath does not exist or contains no subfolders. Verify the path is correct.
Response is very large - Reduce maxDepth or set includeFiles to false to limit the response size.
Missing files in output - Hidden files (starting with '.') and .meta files are automatically excluded.

createScript.fullDescription: Creates a new C# script file in the Unity project. Supports several built-in templates: MonoBehaviour (with Start/Update methods), ScriptableObject (with CreateAssetMenu attribute), EditorWindow (with menu item and OnGUI), and a plain class template for other cases. You can also provide fully custom script content by setting the template to 'Custom' and supplying the 'content' parameter. The .cs extension is automatically appended if not present. IMPORTANT: Creating a .cs file triggers Unity's script compilation and Domain Reload, which will temporarily interrupt the editor. The AssetDatabase.Refresh() is deferred via EditorApplication.delayCall to ensure the MCP response is sent before the reload occurs.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Folder path where the script will be created.
parameters.constraints: Must start with 'Assets'. The folder will be created automatically if it does not exist.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the script. The .cs extension is added automatically if not included.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid C# class name (no spaces, must start with a letter or underscore). Do not include .cs extension.

parameters.name: template
parameters.description: Script template to use. Determines the base class and boilerplate code.
parameters.constraints: Must be one of: 'MonoBehaviour', 'ScriptableObject', 'EditorWindow', 'Custom'. Any other value generates a plain class.

parameters.name: content
parameters.description: Custom script content. Only used when template is set to 'Custom'.
parameters.constraints: Only applicable when template is 'Custom'. Must be valid C# source code.

workflows: Use createFolder to set up a directory structure, then createScript to add scripts to the appropriate folders.
Create a MonoBehaviour script with createScript, then use scene/gameObject tools to attach it to a GameObject.
Create a ScriptableObject script with createScript, then use createAsset (from asset tools) to create instances of it.
Create an EditorWindow script to build custom Unity editor tools for the project.
createScript.unityVersionNotes: Creating scripts triggers Domain Reload in all Unity versions. In Unity 2019.3+, Enter Play Mode Options can be configured to skip Domain Reload during play mode entry, but script compilation still triggers it in the editor.
commonErrors: Error: 'Path and name are required' - Both 'path' and 'name' parameters must be provided and non-empty.
Compilation error after creation - The generated script may have issues if the class name conflicts with existing types. Ensure unique names.
Domain Reload interruption - After creating a script, Unity will recompile and reload the domain. This is normal and expected. The response is sent before the reload occurs.
EditorWindow scripts must be in an Editor folder - If using the 'EditorWindow' template, place the script in an 'Editor' folder (e.g., Assets/Editor) or it will cause build errors.
Custom template with invalid C# - When using template='Custom', ensure the content parameter contains valid C# code, otherwise compilation will fail.

createNewScene.fullDescription: Creates a new empty Unity scene and optionally populates it with default objects (Main Camera with AudioListener and Directional Light). If a name is provided, the scene is saved to 'Assets/{name}.unity' and the AssetDatabase is refreshed. If no name is provided, an unsaved new scene is created in memory. The new scene replaces the currently open scene (Single mode).

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: Name of the new scene. Used as the filename when saving (saved to Assets/{name}.unity).
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid filename without path separators or special characters. Do not include the .unity extension.

parameters.name: addDefaultObjects
parameters.description: Whether to add default objects (Main Camera at position (0,1,-10) with AudioListener, and a Directional Light rotated at (50,-30,0)) to the new scene.

workflows: Create a new scene then use gameObject tools (e.g. createGameObject) to populate it with objects.
Create a new scene, add objects, then call saveScene to persist changes.
Create an empty scene (addDefaultObjects=false) for procedural generation, then add camera and lights manually with createGameObject.
commonErrors: Scene name contains invalid characters (e.g. '/', '\', ':') causing save to fail. Use only alphanumeric characters, underscores, and hyphens.
A scene file with the same name already exists at Assets/{name}.unity and will be overwritten without warning.
Unsaved changes in the current scene are lost when creating a new scene since it uses NewSceneMode.Single. Call saveScene first if needed.

openScene.fullDescription: Opens an existing Unity scene file from disk by its asset path. The scene replaces the currently active scene. Returns the scene name, path, and root object count on success. The path must point to a valid .unity file within the project's Assets folder.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path to the scene file, relative to the project root (e.g. 'Assets/Scenes/MyScene.unity').
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid path to an existing .unity file within the project. Use forward slashes as path separators.

workflows: Open a scene then use getSceneHierarchy to inspect its contents before making modifications.
Save the current scene with saveScene, then open a different scene to work on it.
Open a scene, modify GameObjects, then call saveScene to persist changes.
commonErrors: Path is empty or null: 'Scene path is required'. Always provide a non-empty path.
Scene file does not exist at the specified path. Verify the path using asset/file tools first.
Path uses backslashes instead of forward slashes. Use 'Assets/Scenes/MyScene.unity' format.
Unsaved changes in the current scene are lost when opening a new scene. Call saveScene first if needed.

saveScene.fullDescription: Saves the currently active scene to disk. If a path is provided, the scene is saved to that location (Save As). If no path is provided, the scene is saved to its current location. Returns whether the save was successful and the final scene path.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path to save the scene to. If omitted, saves to the scene's current path. Use this to 'Save As' to a new location.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid asset path ending in .unity if provided. Parent directories must exist.

workflows: After modifying GameObjects in a scene, call saveScene to persist all changes.
Use saveScene with a path to create a copy of the current scene (Save As).
Before opening a different scene, call saveScene to avoid losing unsaved changes.
commonErrors: Saving fails if the scene has never been saved and no path is provided. Provide an explicit path for new unsaved scenes.
Save fails if the target directory does not exist. Ensure the parent folder exists before saving.
Path does not end with .unity extension, which may cause Unity to fail or save in an unexpected format.

getSceneInfo.fullDescription: Retrieves detailed information about the currently active scene, including its name, file path, loaded state, dirty (unsaved changes) flag, root GameObject count, build index, and resolution information (Game view size, default screen size, fullscreen mode).
workflows: Call getSceneInfo to check if a scene has unsaved changes (isDirty) before performing operations that would discard them.
Use getSceneInfo to verify which scene is currently open before modifying objects.
Check buildIndex to see if the scene is included in Build Settings (-1 means not included).
commonErrors: Returns info for the active scene only. If multiple scenes are loaded additively, only the active scene info is returned.
buildIndex returns -1 if the scene has not been added to File > Build Settings.

getSceneHierarchy.fullDescription: Returns the full hierarchy of GameObjects in the current scene as a JSON tree. The output is compact: only non-default values are included (e.g. 'active' only appears if false, 'tag' only if not 'Untagged', 'layer' only if not 'Default'). Use maxDepth to limit traversal depth for large scenes to reduce response size. When maxDepth truncates children, a 'childrenCount' field indicates how many children were hidden. Optionally includes component names and transform info (position, scale, RectTransform size) on each GameObject. Use rootPath to query only a subtree instead of the entire scene.

parameters.name: includeInactive
parameters.description: Whether to include inactive GameObjects in the hierarchy output.

parameters.name: maxDepth
parameters.description: Maximum depth to traverse. 0 = root objects only, 1 = root + direct children, -1 = unlimited depth. Use 2-3 for large scenes to keep response size manageable.
parameters.constraints: Integer value. -1 for unlimited, 0 or positive for depth limit.

parameters.name: includeComponents
parameters.description: Whether to include the list of component type names on each GameObject (excluding Transform which is always present). Increases response size significantly.

parameters.name: includeTransform
parameters.description: Whether to include transform data (position, scale, RectTransform sizeDelta/anchoredPosition) on each node. Position is compact 'x,y,z' format. Scale only shown if not (1,1,1). UI nodes include size and anchoredPos.

parameters.name: rootPath
parameters.description: Path to a root GameObject to query only its subtree. If not provided, queries the entire scene. Useful for inspecting specific UI panels or object groups.
parameters.constraints: Must match an existing GameObject path in the scene.

workflows: Call getSceneHierarchy with maxDepth=0 first to get an overview of root objects, then increase depth for specific subtrees if needed.
Use getSceneHierarchy with includeComponents=true to understand what components are attached before modifying objects.
Use includeTransform=true to see positions and sizes of UI elements when laying out a UI.
Use rootPath to inspect only a specific subtree (e.g. 'Canvas') without loading the entire scene hierarchy.
After creating or modifying GameObjects, call getSceneHierarchy to verify the scene structure is correct.
For large scenes, start with maxDepth=1 and includeComponents=false to get a manageable overview, then drill deeper as needed.
commonErrors: Using maxDepth=-1 with includeComponents=true on a large scene can produce a very large response that may exceed token limits. Start with limited depth.
Objects hidden by maxDepth are indicated by 'childrenCount' in the output. Increase maxDepth or target specific objects to see them.
Null components (missing scripts) are silently skipped in the component list. If a GameObject has missing script references, they will not appear.
rootPath not found: The specified path does not match any GameObject. Check the path using getSceneHierarchy without rootPath first.

findShader.fullDescription: Finds a shader by its exact name and returns detailed information including whether the shader is supported on the current platform, its render queue value, pass count, and asset path. Uses Shader.Find() internally, which requires the exact shader name including category path (e.g. 'Universal Render Pipeline/Lit', not just 'Lit'). Returns found=false if no shader matches the given name.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The exact name of the shader to find, including its category path (e.g. 'Standard', 'Universal Render Pipeline/Lit').
parameters.constraints: Must be the full shader name as it appears in Unity. Case-sensitive. Use listShaders to discover available shader names.

workflows: Use findShader to verify a shader exists before calling setMaterialShader or createMaterial with that shader name.
Use findShader to check if a shader is supported on the current platform (isSupported field) before assigning it to materials.
Use findShader to get the asset path of a custom shader for inspection or duplication.
findShader.unityVersionNotes: In URP/HDRP projects, built-in shaders like 'Standard' may not be available. Use render-pipeline-specific shaders instead (e.g. 'Universal Render Pipeline/Lit').
commonErrors: Shader name is empty or null: 'Shader name is required'. Always provide a non-empty name string.
Shader not found: The name must exactly match the shader name including category path. Use listShaders to find the correct name.
Using a short name like 'Lit' instead of the full path 'Universal Render Pipeline/Lit'. Always use the complete shader name.

listShaders.fullDescription: Lists all shader assets available in the project by searching the AssetDatabase with 't:Shader'. Results can be filtered by a substring match on the shader name. Hidden shaders (those with names starting with 'Hidden/') are excluded by default but can be included with the includeHidden flag. Returns the count and a list of shaders sorted alphabetically by name, each with its name, asset path, and isSupported status.

parameters.name: filter
parameters.description: Optional substring to filter shader names. Only shaders whose name contains this string will be returned. Case-sensitive.
parameters.constraints: Case-sensitive substring match using String.Contains().

parameters.name: includeHidden
parameters.description: Whether to include hidden shaders (those with names starting with 'Hidden/') in the results.

workflows: Call listShaders to discover available shader names before using findShader, setMaterialShader, or createMaterial.
Use listShaders with a filter to find render-pipeline-specific shaders (e.g. filter='Universal Render Pipeline').
