List all shaders including hidden ones to find internal or utility shaders for advanced use cases.
listShaders.unityVersionNotes: The available shaders depend on the render pipeline configured in the project. URP projects will have 'Universal Render Pipeline/*' shaders, HDRP will have 'HDRP/*' shaders.
commonErrors: Filter is case-sensitive: 'universal' will not match 'Universal Render Pipeline/Lit'. Use the exact casing.
Only shaders that exist as assets in the project are listed. Built-in shaders not imported as assets may not appear. Use findShader to check for built-in shaders by name.
Large projects may return many shaders. Use a filter to narrow results.

getMaterialShader.fullDescription: Retrieves the shader currently assigned to a material asset. Returns the material name, its asset path, the shader name, whether the shader is supported on the current platform, and the material's render queue value. The material is loaded from the AssetDatabase using the provided path.

parameters.name: materialPath
parameters.description: Path to the material asset, relative to the project root.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid asset path to an existing .mat file within the project. Use forward slashes as path separators.

workflows: Use getMaterialShader to inspect the current shader on a material before changing it with setMaterialShader.
Check shaderIsSupported to verify the material's shader works on the target platform.
Use getMaterialShader to audit materials and find ones using deprecated or incorrect shaders.
commonErrors: Material path is empty or null: 'Material path is required'. Always provide a non-empty path.
Material not found at the specified path. Verify the path exists using asset search tools. Ensure the path starts with 'Assets/' and ends with '.mat'.
Path uses backslashes instead of forward slashes. Use 'Assets/Materials/MyMaterial.mat' format.

setMaterialShader.fullDescription: Changes the shader assigned to a material asset. The operation is recorded for Undo support. After setting the shader, the material is marked dirty and assets are saved. Returns the material name, old shader name, new shader name, and a success message. Note: changing a shader may reset material property values if the new shader has different properties.

parameters.name: materialPath
parameters.description: Path to the material asset, relative to the project root.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid asset path to an existing .mat file within the project.

parameters.name: shaderName
parameters.description: The exact name of the shader to assign to the material.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid shader name that exists in the project. Use findShader or listShaders to verify the shader name.

workflows: Use getMaterialShader to check the current shader, then setMaterialShader to change it, and getMaterialProperties to verify the new properties.
Use findShader to verify the target shader exists and is supported, then setMaterialShader to assign it.
When migrating materials between render pipelines, use listShaders to find equivalent shaders, then setMaterialShader to reassign.
setMaterialShader.unityVersionNotes: Changing from a built-in shader to a URP/HDRP shader (or vice versa) may cause property values to be lost since property names differ between pipelines.
commonErrors: Material path or shader name is empty: 'Material path and shader name are required'. Both parameters must be provided.
Material not found at the specified path. Verify the material exists using asset search tools.
Shader not found: The shader name must exactly match an available shader. Use listShaders or findShader to verify.
After changing shader, material properties may be reset. Use getMaterialProperties to check and setMaterialProperty to restore values.

getMaterialProperties.fullDescription: Retrieves all properties of a material, including their types, descriptions, and current values. For each shader property, the type (Color, Vector, Float, Range, TexEnv) and current value are returned. Range properties include min/max limits. Texture properties include the texture asset path, name, offset, and scale. Additionally, a synthetic '_RenderQueue' property is included showing the material's render queue value. Returns the material name, shader name, and a dictionary of all properties keyed by property name.

parameters.name: materialPath
parameters.description: Path to the material asset, relative to the project root.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid asset path to an existing .mat file within the project.

workflows: Call getMaterialProperties before setMaterialProperty to discover available property names and their types.
Use getMaterialProperties to audit a material's current configuration, then use setMaterialProperty to adjust values.
After calling setMaterialShader, use getMaterialProperties to see the new shader's available properties.
Use getMaterialProperties to read current color, texture, and float values for documentation or scripting purposes.
commonErrors: Material path is empty or null: 'Material path is required'. Always provide a non-empty path.
Material not found at the specified path. Verify the path exists and points to a .mat file.
Some properties may appear with internal names (e.g. '_MainTex', '_Color', '_BumpMap'). These are the names to use with setMaterialProperty.

setMaterialProperty.fullDescription: Sets a specific property on a material. Supports all shader property types: Color (as {r,g,b,a} object), Vector (as {x,y,z,w} or {x,y,z} object), Float and Range (as a number), and Texture (as an asset path string). First attempts to set the property using PropertyHelper for advanced handling. If that fails, falls back to direct material property setting based on the shader's property type definition. The operation is recorded for Undo support. The material is marked dirty and saved after the change. IMPORTANT: Use getMaterialProperties first to discover available properties and their types.

parameters.name: materialPath
parameters.description: Path to the material asset, relative to the project root.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid asset path to an existing .mat file within the project.

parameters.name: propertyName
parameters.description: The shader property name to set. Must match a property defined in the material's shader. Use getMaterialProperties to list available properties.
parameters.constraints: Must be an exact property name from the shader (typically prefixed with underscore). Use getMaterialProperties to discover valid names.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value to set. Format depends on the property type: Color as {r,g,b,a} object, Vector as {x,y,z,w} object, Float/Range as a number, Texture as an asset path string.
parameters.constraints: Must match the expected format for the property type. Color/Vector must be JSON objects with the correct fields. Float/Range must be a number. Texture must be a valid asset path string.

workflows: Call getMaterialProperties to list available properties and their types, then use setMaterialProperty to set the desired value.
Create a material with createMaterial, then use setMaterialProperty multiple times to configure its appearance (color, metallic, textures, etc.).
Use getMaterialProperties to read a property's current value, modify it, then write it back with setMaterialProperty.
After changing a material's shader with setMaterialShader, use getMaterialProperties then setMaterialProperty to configure the new shader's properties.
commonErrors: Material path or property name is empty: 'Material path and property name are required'. Both must be provided.
Material not found at the specified path. Verify the material exists.
Material does not have the specified property. Use getMaterialProperties to discover valid property names for the material's shader.
Value format mismatch: Color properties require {r,g,b,a} objects, not strings or numbers. Float properties require numbers, not objects.
Texture path is invalid or texture not found at the specified path. Verify the texture asset exists before assigning it.
Could not determine property type: The property name exists on the material but is not recognized by ShaderUtil. This can happen with dynamically added properties.

createMaterial.fullDescription: Creates a new material asset with the specified shader and saves it to the given path. If the path does not end with '.mat', the extension is appended automatically. If the target directory does not exist, it is created automatically. The material is created, saved to disk, and the AssetDatabase is refreshed. Returns the success status, final path, material name, and shader name.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: Path where the material will be saved, relative to the project root. The '.mat' extension is appended automatically if missing.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid asset path within the project. Parent directories will be created if they do not exist.

parameters.name: shaderName
parameters.description: Name of the shader to use for the new material. Defaults to 'Standard' if not provided.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid shader name that exists in the project. Use findShader or listShaders to verify.

workflows: Create a material with createMaterial, then use setMaterialProperty to configure its color, textures, and other properties.
Use listShaders to find the correct shader name, then createMaterial with that shader, then setMaterialProperty to customize it.
Create a material, configure its properties, then assign it to a GameObject's Renderer component using setComponent.
createMaterial.unityVersionNotes: The default shader 'Standard' is only available in built-in render pipeline projects. For URP projects, use 'Universal Render Pipeline/Lit'. For HDRP, use 'HDRP/Lit'.
commonErrors: Path is empty: 'Path is required'. Always provide a non-empty path.
Shader not found: The specified shader name does not exist. Use findShader to verify the shader name before creating the material.
A material already exists at the specified path and will be overwritten without warning.
In URP/HDRP projects, the default 'Standard' shader may not be available, causing creation to fail. Specify an appropriate shader name for your render pipeline.

getShaderProperties.fullDescription: Retrieves all properties defined by a shader, including their names, descriptions, types, and whether they are hidden. For Range-type properties, the minimum value, maximum value, and default value are also included. Returns the shader name, isSupported status, render queue, pass count, total property count, and the full list of properties. This tool inspects the shader definition itself, not a specific material instance. Use getMaterialProperties to get actual values from a material.

parameters.name: shaderName
parameters.description: The exact name of the shader whose properties should be listed.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid shader name that exists in the project. Case-sensitive.

workflows: Use getShaderProperties to inspect a shader's available properties before creating a material with that shader.
Compare properties between two shaders by calling getShaderProperties for each, to plan a shader migration.
Use getShaderProperties to discover property names and types, then use setMaterialProperty with the correct names and value formats.
Check the hidden flag to identify which properties are internal and which are user-facing.
commonErrors: Shader name is empty or null: 'Shader name is required'. Always provide a non-empty name.
Shader not found: The shader name must exactly match an available shader, including its full category path.
This tool shows shader-defined properties, not material instance values. Use getMaterialProperties to see actual values on a specific material.

validateScene.fullDescription: Validates the currently active scene for common issues including missing scripts, broken prefab connections, duplicate GameObject names, and empty GameObjects. Scans all GameObjects in the scene and reports issues categorized by type and severity (Error, Warning, Info). Useful for quality assurance before builds or scene commits.

parameters.name: checkMissingScripts
parameters.description: Check for GameObjects that have components with missing (deleted or unresolved) scripts.

parameters.name: checkMissingPrefabs
parameters.description: Check for GameObjects that are part of a prefab instance but whose source prefab asset is missing.

parameters.name: checkDuplicateNames
parameters.description: Check for multiple GameObjects sharing the same name in the scene. Reports groups of duplicates with their hierarchy paths.

parameters.name: checkEmptyGameObjects
parameters.description: Check for GameObjects that only have a Transform component and no children. These are often leftover placeholders.

workflows: Run validateScene before building to catch broken references, then use findMissingScripts for a deeper scan including prefabs.
Use validateScene with checkDuplicateNames to audit naming conventions, then manually rename objects via scene hierarchy tools.
Combine validateScene (checkEmptyGameObjects: true) with cleanupEmptyFolders to clean up both scene and project structure.
validateScene.unityVersionNotes: PrefabUtility.GetPrefabInstanceStatus is available in Unity 2018.3+. Earlier versions may not detect missing prefab connections correctly.
commonErrors: No active scene loaded: Ensure a scene is open in the editor before running validation.
Large scene causes slow execution: Disable checks you do not need (e.g., checkDuplicateNames) to speed up validation on scenes with thousands of objects.
False positives for duplicate names: Unity allows duplicate names by design; this check is informational and should be reviewed manually.

validateAssets.fullDescription: Validates project assets under a specified path for issues such as missing dependencies (broken references between assets). Iterates through all assets found via AssetDatabase.FindAssets, checks each asset's direct dependencies, and reports any dependency files that do not exist on disk. The unused asset detection feature is declared but not fully implemented and will return an informational message.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The root asset folder path to validate. Must be a valid Unity asset path starting with 'Assets'.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid folder path within the Unity project Assets directory.

parameters.name: checkMissingReferences
parameters.description: Check for assets that reference other assets which no longer exist on disk (broken dependencies).

parameters.name: checkUnusedAssets
parameters.description: Check for assets that are not referenced by any other asset. Note: this feature is not fully implemented and will return an informational message.

workflows: Run validateAssets on a specific folder after moving or renaming assets to detect broken references, then use manageAsset (import) to reimport affected assets.
Use validateAssets with checkMissingReferences before a production build to ensure no broken dependencies ship.
Combine validateAssets with findAssets to first locate assets of a certain type, then validate their integrity.
commonErrors: Invalid path: The path must start with 'Assets' and correspond to an existing folder in the project.
Slow execution on large projects: Scanning the entire Assets folder with checkMissingReferences can be slow on projects with thousands of assets. Narrow the path to a specific subfolder.
checkUnusedAssets returns informational message: This feature is not fully implemented. It requires analyzing all scenes and prefabs which is computationally expensive.

findMissingScripts.fullDescription: Searches for all GameObjects that have one or more missing (null) script components. By default, only the currently loaded scene is scanned. When searchInPrefabs is enabled, all prefab assets in the project are also loaded and checked recursively (including children). Returns a list of objects with missing scripts, including their names, hierarchy paths (for scene objects) or asset paths (for prefabs), and their source.

parameters.name: searchInPrefabs
parameters.description: When true, also searches through all prefab assets in the project in addition to the current scene. Prefabs are checked recursively including all child GameObjects.

workflows: Run findMissingScripts with searchInPrefabs: true after deleting or renaming script files to find all affected GameObjects and prefabs.
Use validateScene first for a quick overview, then run findMissingScripts with searchInPrefabs: true for a thorough project-wide scan.
After resolving missing scripts, run findMissingScripts again to verify all issues are fixed before committing changes.
commonErrors: Slow execution with searchInPrefabs enabled: Loading every prefab in a large project can be time-consuming. Use this option only when a thorough scan is needed.
Missing scripts caused by deleted .cs files: If a MonoBehaviour script file is deleted, any GameObjects referencing it will show missing scripts. Restore the script or remove the component.
Missing scripts caused by assembly definition changes: Moving scripts between assembly definitions can break references. Ensure asmdef files are configured correctly.

cleanupEmptyFolders.fullDescription: Finds and optionally removes empty folders from the Unity project's asset directory. Recursively traverses the folder structure starting from the specified path, ignoring .meta files when determining if a folder is empty. By default runs in dry-run mode (reporting only). When dryRun is set to false, empty folders are deleted via AssetDatabase.DeleteAsset and the AssetDatabase is refreshed. The root 'Assets' folder itself is never deleted even if empty.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The root folder path to start scanning for empty folders. Must be a valid Unity asset path.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid folder path within the Unity project Assets directory.

parameters.name: dryRun
parameters.description: When true, only reports empty folders without deleting them. When false, actually deletes the empty folders from the project.

workflows: First run cleanupEmptyFolders with dryRun: true to review which folders would be deleted, then run again with dryRun: false to perform the actual cleanup.
After bulk-deleting assets, run cleanupEmptyFolders to remove the leftover empty directories.
Use cleanupEmptyFolders as part of a project maintenance routine alongside validateAssets and optimizeTextures.
commonErrors: Folders containing only .meta files are treated as empty: Unity generates .meta files for folders, but these are ignored when checking emptiness. This is the intended behavior.
Version control conflicts: Deleting folders may cause issues if other team members have files in those folders that haven't been synced. Always sync before running with dryRun: false.
Path does not exist: If the specified path does not correspond to an existing directory on disk, the tool will return zero empty folders without error.

optimizeTextures.fullDescription: Scans texture assets under a specified path and checks their import settings for optimization opportunities. Detects three categories of issues: oversized textures (dimensions exceeding the specified maxSize), uncompressed textures (TextureImporterCompression.Uncompressed), and textures with mipmaps disabled on Default texture type (which can cause rendering quality loss for 3D textures viewed at varying distances). Returns the total number of textures checked and a list of issues with their severity levels.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The asset folder path to scan for textures. All Texture2D assets under this path will be checked.
parameters.constraints: Must be a valid folder path within the Unity project Assets directory.

parameters.name: maxSize
parameters.description: The maximum recommended texture dimension in pixels. Textures with width or height exceeding this value will be flagged as oversized.
parameters.constraints: Must be a positive integer. Common values are powers of 2: 512, 1024, 2048, 4096.

workflows: Run optimizeTextures to identify oversized and uncompressed textures before building for mobile platforms where texture memory is limited.
Use findAssets with searchFilter 't:Texture2D' to list all textures first, then run optimizeTextures on specific subfolders to target problem areas.
After importing new art assets, run optimizeTextures to verify import settings meet project standards, then use manageAsset (import) with ForceUpdate to reimport adjusted textures.
optimizeTextures.unityVersionNotes: TextureImporterCompression enum is available in Unity 5.5+. The TextureImporterType.Default value used for mipmap checks corresponds to the standard 3D texture type.
commonErrors: No textures found: Ensure the path is correct and contains Texture2D assets. Non-texture assets in the folder are ignored.
Mipmaps flagged for UI textures: Textures with TextureImporterType set to Sprite or GUI will not be flagged for missing mipmaps since the check only applies to Default type textures.
Large number of issues reported: On projects with many textures, consider narrowing the path to specific folders to get manageable results.
